# 2. ECOR
## 2.1. fliter
```{r}
dat_ecor <- ecor_raw_growth_data %>%
  mutate(
    time = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(time)),
    rep  = factor(rep, levels = rep_levels)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(time), !is.na(od), !is.na(rep), !is.na(carbon), !is.na(strain)) %>%
  filter(od > 0, !time %in% c(1, 2, 3)) %>%
  mutate(
    growth = od > 0.1,
    log10_od = log10(od)
  )
Sys.time()
```
## 2.2. define a function to extract r^2 in curve fitting
```{r}
# Define a custom function to calculate the Coefficient of Determination (R-squared)
# based on the model fit from growthcurver.
calc_r2 <- function(gc) {
  # Return NA if the model failed to converge or does not exist
  if (is.null(gc$model)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  
  # Extract observed OD values (N) from the growthcurver object
  obs <- gc$data$N
  
  # Extract predicted values from the model; handle potential errors during extraction
  pred <- tryCatch(stats::fitted(gc$model), error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # Ensure predicted values exist and match the length of observations
  # Also check for non-zero variance in observations to avoid division by zero
  if (!is.null(pred) && length(obs) == length(pred) && stats::var(obs, na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
    # Calculate Residual Sum of Squares (SS_res)
    ss_res <- sum((obs - pred)^2, na.rm = TRUE)
    # Calculate Total Sum of Squares (SS_tot)
    ss_tot <- sum((obs - mean(obs, na.rm = TRUE))^2, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # R^2 = 1 - (SS_res / SS_tot)
    return(1 - ss_res/ss_tot)
  } else {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
}
Sys.time()
```
## 2.3. execute curve fitting
```{r}
fit_results_ecor <- dat_ecor %>%
  group_by(strain, carbon, rep) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    d <- .x %>% arrange(time)
    n_rows <- nrow(d)
    
    # 1. Calculate rolling median with a 5-point window to smooth noise
    # k=5 includes the target point and two points before/after
    d$rolling_med <- zoo::rollmedian(d$od, k = 5, fill = "extend")
    
    # 2. Identify the maximum rolling median value and its corresponding time
    max_med_val <- max(d$rolling_med, na.rm = TRUE)
    idx_max_med <- which.max(d$rolling_med)
    t_max_med   <- d$time[idx_max_med]
    
    
    # 3. Data pruning: Find the first point that drops below 90% of the maximum rolling median
    # Only data points after the time of maximum growth (t_max_med) are considered
    cutoff_indices <- which(d$time > t_max_med & d$od < (max_med_val * 0.90))
    
    use_data <- d
    is_death_filtered <- FALSE
    
    if (length(cutoff_indices) > 0) {
      # Extract data up to the point just before dropping below the threshold
      cutoff_idx <- min(cutoff_indices)
      use_data <- d[1:(cutoff_idx - 1), ]
      is_death_filtered <- TRUE
    }

    
    # 4. Growth curve fitting using the growthcurver package
    # Note: bg_val subtraction is handled internally by SummarizeGrowth
    gc <- growthcurver::SummarizeGrowth(use_data$time, use_data$od)
    
    
    # 5. Extract standard errors for model parameters if the fit was successful
    se_k <- NA_real_; se_r <- NA_real_; se_n0 <- NA_real_
    if (!is.null(gc$model)) {
      sum_mod <- tryCatch(summary(gc$model)$coefficients, error = function(e) NULL)
      if (!is.null(sum_mod)) {
        # Extract SE by parameter name (k, r, n0)
        if("k" %in% rownames(sum_mod)) se_k <- sum_mod["k", "Std. Error"]
        if("r" %in% rownames(sum_mod)) se_r <- sum_mod["r", "Std. Error"]
        if("n0" %in% rownames(sum_mod)) se_n0 <- sum_mod["n0", "Std. Error"]
      }
    }

    
    # Summarize fit parameters and metadata into a tibble
    dplyr::tibble(
      # Core parameters for curve reconstruction
      k      = gc$vals$k %||% NA_real_,
      n0     = gc$vals$n0 %||% NA_real_,
      r      = gc$vals$r %||% NA_real_,
      bg     = gc$vals$bg %||% 0,         # Returns 0 as internal minimum is subtracted
      # Statistical confidence metrics
      se_k   = se_k,
      se_r   = se_r,
      se_n0  = se_n0,
      r2     = calc_r2(gc),
      # Metadata for analysis and QC
      t_mid  = gc$vals$t_mid %||% NA_real_,
      t_cutoff = max(use_data$time), # Record the end time of the data used
      is_death_filtered = (nrow(use_data) < n_rows),
      od_max = max(.x$od, na.rm = TRUE),
      od_min = min(.x$od, na.rm = TRUE),
      od_ini = use_data$od[1],
      od_max_runmed = max_med_val,
      note   = gc$vals$note %||% NA_character_
    )
  })%>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Classify growth patterns based on OD thresholds and fit results
fit_results_ecor <- fit_results_ecor %>%
  dplyr::mutate(growth_category = case_when(
    is.na(od_max) ~ "Unknown",
    od_max <= 0.1 ~ "No growth",
    !is.na(k) & od_max < 0.8 * k ~ "Slow/Partial growth",
    !is.na(k) & od_max >= 0.8 * k ~ "Growth",
    TRUE ~ "Unclassified"
  ))

Sys.time()

```
## 2.4. reconstruct theoretical datasets using estimated parameters
```{r}
# Generate a smooth time axis within the range of the raw data and calculate predicted OD values.
predict_dat_ecor <- fit_results_ecor %>%
  filter(!is.na(k), !is.na(r), !is.na(n0), !is.na(od_min)) %>%
  group_by(strain, carbon, rep) %>%
  # Create a time column with 0.1 increments for each group up to the cutoff point
  reframe(time = seq(0, t_cutoff, by = 0.1),
          k = k, n0 = n0, r = r, od_min = od_min) %>% # Carry over estimated parameters
  # Apply the logistic growth equation using vectorized operations
  # Formula: OD(t) = min_OD + (K * N0) / (N0 + (K - N0) * e^(-r * t))
  mutate(
    od_pred = od_min + (k * n0) / (n0 + (k - n0) * exp(-r * time))
  )
Sys.time()
```
## 2.5. visualize growth curve (log scale)
```{r, fig.width=16,fig.height=16}
my_vis<-FALSE # Set to TRUE to generate plots
if(my_vis){
  # Iterate through carbon sources for visualization
  for(i in 1:nrow(carbon_df)){
    target_carbon <- carbon_df$carbon[i]
    my_length<-dat_ecor[dat_ecor$carbon==target_carbon,] %>% nrow()
    if(my_length>0){
        p<-ggplot() +
        # Raw Data: Background points representing all replicates in gray
        geom_point(data = dat_ecor %>% filter(carbon == target_carbon), 
                   aes(x = time, y = od), 
                   color = "grey50", alpha = 0.4, size = 0.5) +
        
        # Fitted Curves: Solid lines for each replicate model fit
        geom_line(data = predict_dat_ecor %>% filter(carbon == target_carbon), 
                  aes(x = time, y = od_pred, color = as.factor(rep)), 
                  size = 0.8) +
        
        # Facet by strain to compare growth dynamics across different genetic backgrounds
        facet_wrap(~ strain) +
        
        # Plot styling and axis labeling
        scale_color_manual(values = rep_colors, name = "Replicate") +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = get_breaks(from = 0,to = 80,by = 40))+
        labs(title = paste("Growth Fit - Carbon Source:", target_carbon),
             subtitle = "Dots: Raw Data (Gray), Lines: Model Fits (by Rep)",
             x = "Time (hours)", 
             y = "OD (Absorbance)") +
          
        # Apply log10 transformation to the Y-axis to better visualize the exponential phase
        yscale(.scale ="log10", .format = TRUE)+
          
        # Reference line at OD 0.1 for growth detection threshold
        geom_hline(yintercept = 0.1,color="red",linetype=2)+
        theme_pubr() +
        theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
        
        # Set fixed limits for the log-scaled Y-axis
        p<-ggpar(p,ylim=c(0.03,1))
        print(p)
    }
  }
}


Sys.time()
```

## 2.8. determine best fit
```{r}
best_fit_ecor <- fit_results_ecor %>%
  dplyr::group_by(strain, carbon) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~{
    df   <- .x
    # Identify unique growth categories present in the current group (strain x carbon)
    cats <- unique(df$growth_category)

    if (length(cats) == 1) {
      # Case 1: All replicates share the same category.
      # Select the representative replicate with the highest R-squared value.
      return(df %>% dplyr::slice_max(order_by = r2, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)) 
    } else { 
      # Case 2: Mixed categories within the replicates.
      # Perform a majority vote to determine the consensus growth pattern.
      n_growth   <- sum(df$growth_category == "Growth", na.rm = TRUE)
      n_nogrowth <- sum(df$growth_category == "No growth", na.rm = TRUE)
      n_partial  <- sum(df$growth_category == "Slow/Partial growth", na.rm = TRUE)

      if (n_growth >= 3) {
        # Majority is "Growth": Select the best fit among growth replicates.
        df %>% dplyr::filter(growth_category == "Growth") %>%
          dplyr::slice_max(order_by = r2, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
      } else if (n_nogrowth >= 3) {
        # Majority is "No growth": Select the best fit among no-growth replicates.
        df %>% dplyr::filter(growth_category == "No growth") %>%
          dplyr::slice_max(order_by = r2, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
      } else if (n_partial >= 3) {
        # Majority is "Slow/Partial growth": Select the best fit among partial replicates.
        df %>% dplyr::filter(growth_category == "Slow/Partial growth") %>%
          dplyr::slice_max(order_by = r2, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
      } else { 
        # Case 3: No clear majority (all categories < 3 reps).
        # Mark as "Unstable" and select the replicate with the highest R-squared.
        df %>% dplyr::slice_max(order_by = r2, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
          dplyr::mutate(
            growth_category = "Unstable",
            note = "conflicting reps (no clear majority)"
          )
      }
    }
  }) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

Sys.time()
```
## 2.9. mean and sd in mu_max and od_max
### 2.9.1. use top two r2
```{r}
stat_fit_ecor <- fit_results_ecor %>%
  # 1. Identify target replicates for aggregation within each group
  # Criteria: Must be classified as 'Growth', have a reasonable initial OD (to exclude inoculation errors/bubbles), 
  # and then rank them by R2 in descending order.
  group_by(strain, carbon) %>%
  mutate(
    is_target = growth_category %in% c("Growth", "Slow/Partial growth") & od_ini < 0.07,
    r2_rank = if_else(is_target, min_rank(desc(r2)), NA_integer_)
  ) %>%
  
  # 2. Calculate summary statistics
  summarise(
    n_growth    = sum(growth_category == "Growth", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_no_growth = sum(growth_category == "No growth", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_partial   = sum(growth_category == "Slow/Partial growth", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_total     = n(),
    
    # Store the identifiers (rep) of the selected top 2 replicates as a semicolon-separated string
    selected_rep = paste(rep[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], collapse = "; "),
    
    # Compute mean, median, and SD for r and od_max using only the top 2 ranked replicates
    across(
      c(r, od_max, od_max_runmed),
      list(
        mean   = ~ mean(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE),
        median = ~ median(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE),
        sd     = ~ sd(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # 3. Determine the consensus growth category for the strain-carbon combination
  mutate(growth_category = case_when(
    n_growth >= 3    ~ "Growth",
    n_no_growth >= 3 ~ "No growth",
    n_partial >= 3   ~ "Slow/Partial growth",
    TRUE             ~ "Unstable"
  )) %>%
  
  # 4. Handle "No growth" or missing values by replacing NaN/NA with 0
  mutate(across(
    matches("^(r|od_max)_(mean|median|sd)"),
        ~ case_when(
        n_no_growth > 2 ~ 0,           # Set to 0 if confirmed as No Growth
        is.nan(.x)      ~ 0,           # Set to 0 if no valid replicates were found
        is.na(.x)       ~ 0,           # Set to 0 if SD calculation resulted in NA
        TRUE            ~ .x
      )
  ))

# Merge with existing best-fit results for comparison
my_tmp<-best_fit_ecor %>% select(strain,carbon,r,r2,growth_category) %>% 
  rename(r_bh=r,r2_bh=r2,growth_category_bh=growth_category)

stat_fit_ecor<-stat_fit_ecor %>% left_join(my_tmp,by=c("strain","carbon"))

Sys.time()
```

## 2.12. Summary
### 2.12.1. Strains
```{r, fig.height=4, fig.width=12,dpi=300}
# 1. & 2. Summarize the growth categories per strain using count and pivot_wider
my_df <- stat_fit_ecor %>%
  group_by(strain, growth_category) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Spread categories into columns to handle the sorting logic
  pivot_wider(names_from = growth_category, values_from = Count, values_fill = 0)

# 3. Sort strains by the number of "Growth" cases (descending)
# Note: Ensure "Growth" column exists even if all values are zero
if(!"Growth" %in% colnames(my_df)) my_df$Growth <- 0
my_levels <- my_df %>% arrange(desc(Growth)) %>% pull(strain)
my_df$strain <- factor(my_df$strain, levels = my_levels)

# 4. & 5. Reshape to long format and refine Category names/levels for plotting
my_df <- my_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -strain, names_to = "Category", values_to = "Count") %>%
  mutate(Category = factor(Category, 
                           levels = c("No growth", "Growth", "Slow/Partial growth", "Unstable")))

# 6. Generate a stacked bar plot showing the growth profile of each strain
ggbarplot(my_df,x="strain",y="Count",
          fill = "Category",linewidth=0,
          palette = gr_ctlg_colors,
          xlab="Strain",ylab="Number of carbon sources",
          legend.title="Growth category")+
  rotate_x_text(angle = 90)
Sys.time()
```
### 2.12.2. Carbon sources
```{r, fig.height=3, fig.width=7,dpi=300}
# 1. & 2. Aggregate growth categories per carbon source using tidyverse functions
# This replaces the manual for-loop with a more efficient grouping and pivoting approach.
my_df <- stat_fit_ecor %>%
  group_by(carbon, growth_category) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Pivot to wide format to handle sorting and ensure all categories are represented
  pivot_wider(names_from = growth_category, values_from = Count, values_fill = 0)

# Ensure "Growth" column exists for sorting even if it contains no counts
if(!"Growth" %in% colnames(my_df)) my_df$Growth <- 0

# 3. Sort carbon sources based on the number of strains that successfully utilized them
my_levels <- my_df %>% arrange(desc(Growth)) %>% pull(carbon)
my_df$carbon <- factor(my_df$carbon, levels = my_levels)
```

### 2.15.1. use all replicates
```{r}
stat_fit_ecor_allrep <- fit_results_ecor %>%
  # 1. Identify target replicates (Top-2 selection and all-target selection)
  group_by(strain, carbon) %>%
  mutate(
    is_target = growth_category %in% c("Growth", "Slow/Partial growth") & od_ini < 0.07,
    r2_rank   = if_else(is_target, min_rank(desc(r2)), NA_integer_)
  ) %>%
  
  # 2. Compute summary statistics
  summarise(
    n_growth    = sum(growth_category == "Growth", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_no_growth = sum(growth_category == "No growth", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_partial   = sum(growth_category == "Slow/Partial growth", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_total     = n(),
    
    # [Top 2] IDs of selected replicates
    selected_rep = paste(rep[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], collapse = "; "),
    # [All] IDs of all qualifying replicates
    selected_rep_all = paste(rep[is_target], collapse = "; "),
    
    # [Top 2] Mean, median, and SD computed from the top-2 replicates only
    across(
      c(r, od_max, od_max_runmed),
      list(
        mean   = ~ mean(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE),
        median = ~ median(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE),
        sd     = ~ sd(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE),
        cv     = ~ sd(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE) / mean(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    ),
    
    # [All] Mean, median, and SD computed from all qualifying replicates (is_target == TRUE)
    across(
      c(r, od_max, od_max_runmed),
      list(
        mean   = ~ mean(.x[is_target], na.rm = TRUE),
        median = ~ median(.x[is_target], na.rm = TRUE),
        sd     = ~ sd(.x[is_target], na.rm = TRUE),
        cv     = ~ sd(.x[is_target], na.rm = TRUE) / mean(.x[is_target], na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}_all"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # 3. Assign growth category (using the same criteria as before)
  mutate(growth_category = case_when(
    n_growth >= 3    ~ "Growth",
    n_no_growth >= 3 ~ "No growth",
    n_partial >= 3   ~ "Slow/Partial growth",
    TRUE             ~ "Unstable"
  )) %>%
  
  # 4. Replace "No growth" and missing values (NaN/NA) with 0
  #    (applied to both Top-2 and All columns)
  mutate(across(
    matches("^(r|od_max)_(mean|median|sd)(_all)?$"),
    ~ case_when(
      n_no_growth > 2 ~ 0,
      is.nan(.x)      ~ 0,
      is.na(.x)       ~ 0,
      TRUE            ~ .x
    )
  ))

# Join with the existing best-fit data (unchanged)

  rename(r_bh = r, r2_bh = r2, growth_category_bh = growth_category)

stat_fit_ecor_allrep <- stat_fit_ecor_allrep %>% left_join(my_tmp, by = c("strain", "carbon"))
```

# 3. MA
## 3.1. fliter
```{r}
dat_ma <-bind_rows(ma_anc_raw_growth_data,ma_round_raw_growth_data) %>%
  filter(time %nin% c(1,2,3)) %>%
  mutate(log10_od=log10(od)) %>%
  mutate(rep=factor(rep, levels = rep_levels))
Sys.time()
```
## 3.2. execute curve fitting
```{r}
# Fit growth models using SummarizeGrowth for each combination of colony, carbon source, round, and replicate
fit_results_ma <- dat_ma %>%
  group_by(colony, carbon, round, rep,colony_round,lineage) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    d <- .x %>% arrange(time)
    n_rows <- nrow(d)
    
    
    # 1. Smooth OD data using a rolling median (window size k=5)
    # This helps mitigate high-frequency noise in the growth curve
    d$rolling_med <- zoo::rollmedian(d$od, k = 5, fill = "extend")
    
    # 2. Identify the peak of the smoothed growth curve
    max_med_val <- max(d$rolling_med, na.rm = TRUE)
    idx_max_med <- which.max(d$rolling_med)
    t_max_med   <- d$time[idx_max_med]
    
    
    # 3. Data pruning (Cutoff determination)
    # Identify the first point where OD drops below 90% of the rolling median maximum
    # only considering time points after the peak (t_max_med) to avoid fitting death phases.
    cutoff_indices <- which(d$time > t_max_med & d$od < (max_med_val * 0.90))
    
    use_data <- d
    is_death_filtered <- FALSE
    
    if (length(cutoff_indices) > 0) {
      # Prune dataset to keep only the growth phase up to the cutoff point
      cutoff_idx <- min(cutoff_indices)
      use_data <- d[1:(cutoff_idx - 1), ]
      is_death_filtered <- TRUE
    }

    
    # 4. Perform logistic growth curve fitting
    gc <- growthcurver::SummarizeGrowth(use_data$time, use_data$od)
    
    
    # 5. Extract standard errors (SE) for parameters k, r, and n0 if model converged
    se_k <- NA_real_; se_r <- NA_real_; se_n0 <- NA_real_
    if (!is.null(gc$model)) {
      sum_mod <- tryCatch(summary(gc$model)$coefficients, error = function(e) NULL)
      if (!is.null(sum_mod)) {
        if("k" %in% rownames(sum_mod)) se_k <- sum_mod["k", "Std. Error"]
        if("r" %in% rownames(sum_mod)) se_r <- sum_mod["r", "Std. Error"]
        if("n0" %in% rownames(sum_mod)) se_n0 <- sum_mod["n0", "Std. Error"]
      }
    }

    
    # Consolidate parameters and analysis metadata into a tibble
    dplyr::tibble(
      k      = gc$vals$k %||% NA_real_,
      n0     = gc$vals$n0 %||% NA_real_,
      r      = gc$vals$r %||% NA_real_,
      bg     = gc$vals$bg %||% 0,
      se_k   = se_k,
      se_r   = se_r,
      se_n0  = se_n0,
      r2     = calc_r2(gc),
      t_mid  = gc$vals$t_mid %||% NA_real_,
      t_cutoff = max(use_data$time),
      is_death_filtered = (nrow(use_data) < n_rows),
      od_max = max(.x$od, na.rm = TRUE),
      od_min = min(.x$od, na.rm = TRUE),
      od_ini = use_data$od[1],
      od_max_runmed = max_med_val,
      note   = gc$vals$note %||% NA_character_
    )
  })%>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Classify growth based on empirical OD thresholds
fit_results_ma <- fit_results_ma %>%
  dplyr::mutate(growth_category = case_when(
    is.na(od_max) ~ "Unknown",
    od_max <= 0.1 ~ "No growth",
    !is.na(k) & od_max < 0.8 * k ~ "Slow/Partial growth",
    !is.na(k) & od_max >= 0.8 * k ~ "Growth",
    TRUE ~ "Unclassified"
  )) 

# Extract lineage information (Ancestors and Sublineages) from colony strings
fit_results_ma <- fit_results_ma %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Anc = str_extract(colony, "colony[1-3]"),
    sublineage = str_extract(colony, "(?<=_).*$") %>% as.numeric() 
  )
Sys.time()
```
## 3.3. reconstruct theoretical datasets using estimated parameters
```{r}
predict_dat_ma <- fit_results_ma %>%
  filter(!is.na(k), !is.na(r), !is.na(n0), !is.na(od_min)) %>%
  group_by(colony, carbon,round, rep,colony_round,lineage) %>%
  reframe(time = seq(0, t_cutoff, by = 0.1),
          k = k, n0 = n0, r = r, od_min = od_min) %>% 
  mutate(
    od_pred = od_min + (k * n0) / (n0 + (k - n0) * exp(-r * time))
  )
Sys.time()
```

## 3.7. determine best fit
```{r}
best_fit_ma <- fit_results_ma %>%
  # Grouping by experimental units: colony, carbon source, and evolution round
  dplyr::group_by(colony, carbon, round, colony_round,lineage) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~{
    df   <- .x
    # Identify unique growth categories observed across replicates for this group
    cats <- unique(df$growth_category)

    if (length(cats) == 1) {
      # Case 1: All replicates are consistent in their growth category.
      # Select the best representative replicate based on the highest R-squared value.
      return(df %>% dplyr::slice_max(order_by = r2, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)) 
    } else { 
      # Case 2: Inconsistent results across replicates (mixed categories).
      # Determine the consensus category via a majority vote (requires at least 3 reps).
      n_growth   <- sum(df$growth_category == "Growth", na.rm = TRUE)
      n_nogrowth <- sum(df$growth_category == "No growth", na.rm = TRUE)
      n_partial  <- sum(df$growth_category == "Slow/Partial growth", na.rm = TRUE)

      if (n_growth >= 3) {
        # Majority is "Growth": Filter for growth replicates and pick the best fit.
        df %>% dplyr::filter(growth_category == "Growth") %>%
          dplyr::slice_max(order_by = r2, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
      } else if (n_nogrowth >= 3) { 
        # Majority is "No growth": Select the best fit among no-growth replicates.
        df %>% dplyr::filter(growth_category == "No growth") %>%
          dplyr::slice_max(order_by = r2, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
      } else if (n_partial >= 3) { 
        # Majority is "Slow/Partial growth": Select the best fit among partial replicates.
        df %>% dplyr::filter(growth_category == "Slow/Partial growth") %>%
          dplyr::slice_max(order_by = r2, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
      } else {
        # Case 3: No clear majority exists (e.g., highly variable results).
        # Label the group as "Unstable" and select the replicate with the highest R-squared.
        df %>% dplyr::slice_max(order_by = r2, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
          dplyr::mutate(
            growth_category = "Unstable",
            note = "conflicting reps (no clear majority)"
          )
      }
    }
  }) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

Sys.time()
```
## 3.8. mean and sd in mu_max and od_max
### 3.8.1. use top two r2
```{r}
stat_fit_ma <- fit_results_ma %>%
  # 1. Identify target replicates for statistical calculation within each group
  # Criteria: Must show growth/partial growth and have a valid initial OD (excludes errors).
  # Replicates are then ranked by R-squared in descending order.
  group_by(colony, carbon, round, colony_round,lineage) %>%
  mutate(
    is_target = growth_category %in% c("Growth", "Slow/Partial growth") & od_ini < 0.07, 
    r2_rank = if_else(is_target, min_rank(desc(r2)), NA_integer_)
  ) %>%
  
  # 2. Aggregation and statistical summary
  summarise(
    n_growth    = sum(growth_category == "Growth", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_no_growth = sum(growth_category == "No growth", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_partial   = sum(growth_category == "Slow/Partial growth", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_total     = n(),
    
    # Concatenate the identifiers of the selected top 2 replicates
    selected_rep = paste(rep[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], collapse = "; "),
    
    # Calculate mean, median, and SD for key parameters using only the top 2 replicates
    across(
      c(r, od_max, od_max_runmed),
      list(
        mean   = ~ mean(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE),
        median = ~ median(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE),
        sd     = ~ sd(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # 3. Determine consensus growth category for the entire group
  mutate(growth_category = case_when(
    n_growth >= 3    ~ "Growth",
    n_no_growth >= 3 ~ "No growth",
    n_partial >= 3   ~ "Slow/Partial growth",
    TRUE             ~ "Unstable"
  )) %>%
  
  # 4. Handle "No growth" or non-calculable cases by zeroing out parameters
  mutate(across(
    matches("^(r|od_max)_(mean|median|sd)"),
        ~ case_when(
        n_no_growth > 2 ~ 0,           
        is.nan(.x)      ~ 0,           
        is.na(.x)       ~ 0,           
        TRUE            ~ .x
      )
  ))

# Merge with best-fit data and organize lineage metadata
my_tmp<-best_fit_ma %>% select(colony_round,carbon,r,r2,growth_category) %>% 
  rename(r_bh=r,r2_bh=r2,growth_category_bh=growth_category)

stat_fit_ma<-stat_fit_ma %>% 
  left_join(my_tmp,by=c("colony_round","carbon")) %>%
  # 5. Extract and sort lineage information for logical ordering in plots
  mutate(
    Anc = str_extract(colony, "colony[1-3]"), # 冒頭3文字を抽出
    sublineage = str_extract(colony, "(?<=_).*$") %>% as.numeric() # _以降を数値として抽出
  ) %>%
  # Sort by Ancestor, then Sublineage, then Evolution Round
  arrange(Anc, sublineage, round) %>%
  # Fix factor levels for 'colony_round' based on the sorted order
  mutate(
    colony_round = factor(colony_round, levels = unique(colony_round))
  )
```

## 3.11. Summary
### 3.11.1. Colony-Round
```{r, fig.height=4, fig.width=16,dpi=300}
# 1. & 2. Aggregate growth categories per colony_round using tidyverse functions
# This approach is faster and more scalable than manual looping.
my_df <- stat_fit_ma %>%
  group_by(colony_round, growth_category) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Pivot to wide format to handle potential missing categories and maintain consistency
  pivot_wider(names_from = growth_category, values_from = Count, values_fill = 0)

# 3. Preserve the pre-defined factor levels of colony_round
# (Assumes stat_fit_ma was already sorted by Anc/sublineage/round in the previous step)
my_levels <- levels(stat_fit_ma$colony_round)
my_df$colony_round <- factor(my_df$colony_round, levels = my_levels)

# 4. & 5. Reshape to long format and standardize category names/levels for the legend
my_df <- my_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -colony_round, names_to = "Category", values_to = "Count") %>%
  mutate(Category = factor(Category, 
                           levels = c("No growth", "Growth", "Slow/Partial growth", "Unstable")))

# 6. Generate a stacked bar plot to visualize the metabolic profile of each evolutionary timepoint
ggbarplot(my_df, x = "colony_round", y = "Count",
          fill = "Category", linewidth = 0,
          palette = gr_ctlg_colors,
          xlab = "Colony @ Round", ylab = "Number of carbon sources",
          legend.title = "Growth category") +
  rotate_x_text(angle = 90)

Sys.time()
```
### 3.11.2. Carbon sources
```{r, fig.height=4, fig.width=8,dpi=300}
# 1. & 2. Aggregate growth categories per carbon source across all evolutionary lineages
# Using group_by and n() is more efficient and readable than a manual for-loop.
my_df <- stat_fit_ma %>%
  group_by(carbon, growth_category) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Pivot to wide format to simplify the sorting logic and ensure consistency
  pivot_wider(names_from = growth_category, values_from = Count, values_fill = 0)

# 3. Sort carbon sources based on the total number of "Growth" observations
# Ensure the "Growth" column exists to avoid errors in the ordering process
if(!"Growth" %in% colnames(my_df)) my_df$Growth <- 0
my_levels <- my_df %>% arrange(desc(Growth)) %>% pull(carbon)
my_df$carbon <- factor(my_df$carbon, levels = my_levels)

# 4. & 5. Reshape to long format and standardize category names for plotting
my_df <- my_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -carbon, names_to = "Category", values_to = "Count") %>%
  mutate(Category = factor(Category, 
                           levels = c("No growth", "Growth", "Slow/Partial growth", "Unstable")))

# 6. Generate a stacked bar plot to compare carbon source utilization across lineages
ggbarplot(my_df, x = "carbon", y = "Count", 
          fill = "Category", linewidth = 0,
          palette = gr_ctlg_colors,
          xlab = "Carbon sources", ylab = "Number of lineages",
          legend.title = "Growth category", legend = "right") +
  rotate_x_text(angle = 90)

Sys.time()
```

## 3.13. Four reps
### 3.13.1. use all replicates
```{r}
stat_fit_ma_allrep <- fit_results_ma %>%
  # 1. Identify target replicates (Top-2 selection and all-target selection)
  group_by(colony, carbon, round, colony_round, lineage) %>%
  mutate(
    is_target = growth_category %in% c("Growth", "Slow/Partial growth") & od_ini < 0.07, 
    r2_rank   = if_else(is_target, min_rank(desc(r2)), NA_integer_)
  ) %>%
  
  # 2. Compute summary statistics
  summarise(
    n_growth    = sum(growth_category == "Growth", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_no_growth = sum(growth_category == "No growth", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_partial   = sum(growth_category == "Slow/Partial growth", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_total     = n(),
    
    # [Top 2] IDs of selected replicates
    selected_rep = paste(rep[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], collapse = "; "),
    # [Top 2] Mean, median, and SD computed from the top-2 replicates only
    selected_rep_all = paste(rep[is_target], collapse = "; "),
    
    # [Top 2] Mean, median, and SD computed from the top-2 replicates only
    across(
      c(r, od_max, od_max_runmed),
      list(
        mean   = ~ mean(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE),
        median = ~ median(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE),
        sd     = ~ sd(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE),
        cv     = ~ sd(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE) / mean(.x[is_target & r2_rank <= 2], na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    ),
    
    # [All] Mean, median, and SD computed from all qualifying replicates (is_target == TRUE)
    across(
      c(r, od_max, od_max_runmed),
      list(
        mean   = ~ mean(.x[is_target], na.rm = TRUE),
        median = ~ median(.x[is_target], na.rm = TRUE),
        sd     = ~ sd(.x[is_target], na.rm = TRUE),
        cv     = ~ sd(.x[is_target], na.rm = TRUE) / mean(.x[is_target], na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}_all"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # 3. Assign growth category (using the same criteria as before)
  mutate(growth_category = case_when(
    n_growth >= 3    ~ "Growth",
    n_no_growth >= 3 ~ "No growth",
    n_partial >= 3   ~ "Slow/Partial growth",
    TRUE             ~ "Unstable"
  )) %>%
  
  # 4. Replace "No growth" and missing values (NaN/NA) with 0
  #    (applied to both Top-2 and All columns)
  mutate(across(
    matches("^(r|od_max)_(mean|median|sd|cv)(_all)?$"),
    ~ case_when(
      n_no_growth > 2                        ~ 0,
      is.na(.x) | is.nan(.x) | is.infinite(.x) ~ 0,
      TRUE                                   ~ .x
    )
  ))

# Join with the existing best-fit data
my_tmp <- best_fit_ma %>% 
  select(colony_round, carbon, r, r2, growth_category) %>% 
  rename(r_bh = r, r2_bh = r2, growth_category_bh = growth_category)

stat_fit_ma_allrep <- stat_fit_ma_allrep %>% 
  left_join(my_tmp, by = c("colony_round", "carbon")) %>%
  mutate(
    Anc = str_extract(colony, "colony[1-3]"),
    sublineage = str_extract(colony, "(?<=_).*$") %>% as.numeric()
  ) %>%
  arrange(Anc, sublineage, round) %>%
  mutate(
    colony_round = factor(colony_round, levels = unique(colony_round))
  )
```
